indication: Locally advanced or metastatic conventional chondrosarcoma, IDH1-mutant
biomarker: IDH1 R132C/L/G/H/S by central testing on primary or metastatic tissue
endpoint: PFS by blinded independent central review in grade 1 and 2 participants
quality: low risk of bias by design; results not yet reported
inclusion_match_notes: Eligibility reads "conventional chondrosarcoma Grades 1, 2, or 3", and the condition field repeats it, so dedifferentiated histology sits outside the enrolling population — the target_validator read is correct and I confirmed it against the live record. Two further gates would bite even if the histology fit: randomisation requires documented radiographic progression across two imaging assessments, which a newly diagnosed treatment-naive patient has not accrued, and major surgery within 4 weeks is exclusionary, which collides directly with acetabular stabilisation. The registered criteria state no ECOG threshold, so the assumed-2 performance status is not what closes this door.

indication: Advanced chondrosarcoma with IDH1 mutation
design: Multicentre open-label dose-escalation and expansion, chondrosarcoma subgroup
intervention_dosing: 100 mg twice daily to 1,200 mg once daily; 500 mg daily selected
inclusion_match_notes: This is the dataset the whole IDH axis rests on: 21 patients with advanced chondrosarcoma, median PFS 5.6 months, 52% with stable disease, and almost no drug-attributable grade 3 toxicity. Enrollment was written as IDH1-mutant advanced solid tumours rather than a named histology, so dedifferentiated disease was not excluded here — the 2025 long-term report shows 8 of these 21 were non-conventional. The row is informational for this patient because the study is closed, but it is the reason IDH1/IDH2 sequencing outranks every other pending test.

indication: Advanced conventional chondrosarcoma with IDH1 mutation (long-term follow-up)
design: Long-term follow-up of the phase 1 chondrosarcoma subgroup, conventional histology only
endpoint: Objective response rate (conventional chondrosarcoma); median PFS 7.4 months; median DoR 53.5 months
inclusion_match_notes: Of the 21 chondrosarcoma patients, 13 had conventional histology and all reported activity — 23.1% ORR, 53.5-month median duration of response — comes from those 13. The other 8 were non-conventional and were not analysed separately, so how ivosidenib behaves in dedifferentiated disease is unquantified rather than negative. Read alongside the phase 3, the pattern is that the drug is being developed narrowly around the conventional subtype, which is the specific gap this patient falls into.

indication: IDH1-mutant chondrosarcoma, conventional grade 2 or 3
biomarker: IDH1 mutation, CLIA-confirmed; central pathology review
quality: single-arm; accrual stopped at 6 of planned enrolment
inclusion_match_notes: The second IDH1 chondrosarcoma protocol rules her out even more explicitly than the phase 3: "Patients with low grade (grade 1) and dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma are ineligible". Worth noting for contrast that this one does allow ECOG 0-2, so the fitness bar was never the binding constraint on the IDH axis — histology is. It is also closed to accrual with 6 patients enrolled, and it carries the same 4-week major-surgery washout.

indication: IDH2-mutated malignant sinonasal and skull base tumours, including chondrosarcoma
line: 2L+ (prior systemic therapy in the recurrent/metastatic setting required)
inclusion_match_notes: Chondrosarcoma is named in the eligible histologies and the ECOG bar is 0-2, which would suit an assumed-2 patient — but primary tumours must be located in the sinonasal cavity or skull base, and an acetabular primary is not. Prior systemic therapy in the recurrent or metastatic setting is also mandatory, which a treatment-naive patient does not have. The row stays in the dossier because it is the only active IDH2-directed protocol that takes chondrosarcoma at all, so it would matter if an IDH2 mutation turned up and the site restriction were ever waived.

indication: Advanced solid tumours with IDH1 or IDH2 mutations (cholangiocarcinoma, chondrosarcoma, glioma named)
biomarker: IDH1 R132 by tissue or ctDNA (ctDNA accepted for chondrosarcoma)
design: Phase 1 dose escalation and expansion, biomarker-selected basket
inclusion_match_notes: A biomarker-gated basket rather than a histology-gated trial: any solid tumour with IDH1 R132 qualifies, chondrosarcoma is named, and no conventional-versus-dedifferentiated language appears. Two things blunt it — accrual has closed and primary completion passed in 2023, and the ECOG bar is 0-1. One detail worth carrying forward: for chondrosarcoma the protocol accepts ctDNA as well as tissue for the IDH call, which matters because mutant IDH1 is recurrently lost in metastatic evolution and archival pelvic tissue may not describe the lung nodules.

indication: IDH1 or IDH2 mutant solid tumours (non-cholangiocarcinoma, non-CNS)
biomarker: IDH1 or IDH2 mutation with neomorphic activity, CLIA-confirmed
design: Simon two-stage single-arm phase 2, biomarker-selected basket
intervention_dosing: Per NCI protocol; oral PARP plus oral ATR inhibitor
inclusion_match_notes: The mechanism here rides the IDH mutation rather than inhibiting it — 2-HG accumulation produces a homologous-recombination defect that PARP and ATR inhibition are meant to exploit, so an IDH-mutant result would open this door as well as the direct-inhibitor door. Eligibility is tumour-agnostic and CNS tumours are the only histology carve-out. Against it: accrual has closed, ECOG 0-1 is required, progression despite standard therapy is required, and serial biopsies are mandatory unless the PI waives them.

indication: Advanced solid tumours; chondrosarcoma is a named dose-escalation population
line: not specified for the chondrosarcoma population
biomarker: none required for the chondrosarcoma cohort
design: Phase 1 dose escalation and expansion, monotherapy and combinations
intervention: IACS-6274 (glutaminase-1 inhibitor), alone or with bevacizumab and paclitaxel
inclusion_match_notes: Chondrosarcoma is written into Part A dose escalation as its own population, with no subtype restriction and no prior-therapy requirement stated for that group — unusual, and it makes this one of the few open protocols a treatment-naive chondrosarcoma patient is not automatically outside. The metabolic rationale is glutamine dependence, which in this disease travels with IDH mutation, so an IDH result would strengthen rather than gate the case. ECOG must be 0 or 1 with no deterioration in the prior fortnight, which is where an assumed-2 status has to be measured before anything else is discussed.

indication: Advanced chondrosarcoma, all subtypes (88% metastatic)
intervention: Chemotherapy, anthracycline-containing in 131 of 180 (73%); combination regimens in 54.5%
endpoint: RECIST objective response rate by subtype; median PFS 4.7 months; median OS 18 months
quality: retrospective, ROBINS-I serious risk of confounding by indication
inclusion_match_notes: The population is hers: advanced chondrosarcoma, mostly metastatic, treated with anthracycline-based chemotherapy, with response rates split by subtype — 20.5% in dedifferentiated against 11.5% in conventional and 0% in clear-cell. The effect size in this row is the dedifferentiated ORR; whole-cohort median PFS was 4.7 months (95% CI 3.0-6.5) and median OS 18 months. One finding cuts straight at this case: performance status of 2 or worse was independently associated with shorter PFS, so the unmeasured ECOG is prognostic here and not only an eligibility question.

indication: Metastatic or unresectable dedifferentiated liposarcoma, undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma and related poorly differentiated sarcomas
line: 1L (no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease)
intervention_dosing: Doxorubicin IV plus pembrolizumab 200 mg IV q3w
quality: randomised, low risk of bias by design; results pending
inclusion_match_notes: Mechanically this is the pairing her tumour biology argues for — first-line anthracycline plus PD-1 blockade in a chemo-responsive, PD-L1-expressing high-grade sarcoma — and it is one of the few sarcoma protocols that requires patients be treatment-naive rather than pretreated. The histology list is soft-tissue: DDLPS, UPS and a named set of pleomorphic and poorly differentiated soft-tissue diagnoses, with "not limited to" leaving some investigator latitude but no bone-sarcoma entry. She cannot enroll as written, and the ECOG bar is 0-1; the row is here so the board can see what the off-protocol doxorubicin-plus-checkpoint argument would be extrapolating from.

indication: Advanced soft tissue sarcoma, first line
sponsor: Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine
inclusion_match_notes: Included as a documented exclusion rather than an option: the regimen is exactly the doxorubicin-ifosfamide-plus-PD-L1 combination her histology invites, and it requires patients be systemically untreated, which she is — but exclusion criterion 1 names chondrosarcoma explicitly, alongside osteosarcoma and Ewing sarcoma. That pattern repeats across the first-line sarcoma chemo-immunotherapy trials I screened, where the enrolling histology lists are soft-tissue and cartilage tumours are carved out. Recording it stops the same trial being rediscovered and re-proposed downstream.

indication: Advanced bone sarcomas, including 14 chondrosarcoma (10 conventional, 4 dedifferentiated)
intervention_dosing: Sunitinib 37.5 mg/day days 1-14 then 25 mg/day; nivolumab 3 mg/kg q2w
endpoint: 6-month progression-free survival rate by central review
sponsor: Grupo Español de Investigación en Sarcomas (GEIS)
inclusion_match_notes: The registered eligibility names "chondrosarcoma and dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma" outright, which almost no other checkpoint protocol does, and 4 of the 40 patients treated had dedifferentiated disease. Six-month PFS was 42% across bone sarcomas, though subgroup numbers are too small to say what the dedifferentiated patients contributed. The trial is closed, and it required both ECOG 0-1 and progression within the preceding 6 months, so it informs the PD-1 argument rather than offering a seat.

indication: Advanced soft-tissue and bone sarcoma; bone cohort included 5 chondrosarcoma
effect_size: 1 of 5 chondrosarcoma patients (20%) responded; 2 of 40 (5%) in the whole bone cohort
quality: single-arm, primary endpoint not met in either cohort
sponsor: Sarcoma Alliance for Research through Collaboration (SARC)
inclusion_match_notes: The bone cohort took chondrosarcoma without subtype restriction and one of the five patients responded, which is thin evidence but it is the origin of the claim that checkpoint activity in this disease clusters in the dedifferentiated variant. Whether that single responder had dedifferentiated histology is not stated in the primary report. The trial is closed and required up to three prior lines plus a biopsiable lesion, so its value here is as the PD-L1 rationale behind ordering the IHC, not as a route to treatment.

indication: Advanced solid tumours, tissue TMB-high (KEYNOTE-158 biomarker analysis)
line: 2L+ (progression on or intolerance to at least one prior line)
biomarker: tissue TMB >=10 mutations per megabase (FoundationOne CDx)
design: Prospective biomarker analysis within a multi-cohort single-arm phase 2; 790 of 1050 patients evaluable for tissue TMB, 102 tTMB-high
endpoint: Objective response rate by independent central review: 29% (95% CI 21-39) in tTMB-high versus 6% (95% CI 5-8) in non-tTMB-high
quality: non-randomised biomarker analysis; ten named tumour cohorts, none of them sarcoma
inclusion_match_notes: This is the evidence behind the tumour-agnostic TMB-high approval, so it is a live route for her the moment a comprehensive panel returns a TMB and an MSI call — biomarker-defined eligibility, no histology gate. Two caveats to keep visible: chondrosarcoma was not among the ten tumour cohorts analysed, and the pan-tumour TMB-high label reads for previously treated disease, so it would follow first-line chemotherapy rather than replace it. Chondrosarcoma is typically TMB-low, which makes this a low-prior test that costs nothing extra on a panel already being ordered.

indication: Advanced treatment-refractory solid tumours including sarcoma (IDeate-PanTumor01 dose escalation)
biomarker: none required; B7-H3 expression not an entry criterion
endpoint: Safety; antitumour activity by RECIST 1.1 at >=4.8 mg/kg
inclusion_match_notes: B7-H3 is reported in around 96% of dedifferentiated chondrosarcomas, and sarcoma is one of the ten tumour types this pan-tumour protocol enrolls, so the antigen and the histology both line up. What does not line up is the line of therapy and the fitness bar: patients must be refractory to standard treatment and ECOG 0-1, which a treatment-naive patient with an assumed ECOG of 2 fails on both counts today. Note the trial does not require a B7-H3 IHC result to enter, so a negative or absent stain would not itself exclude her later.

indication: Relapsed or refractory osteosarcoma and other sarcomas
biomarker: none required; fresh or archival tissue mandatory
inclusion_match_notes: "Other sarcomas" is the enrolling language, with no exclusion of cartilage histologies, which makes this the most sarcoma-specific B7-H3 protocol running. It is also the one whose entry criteria she currently fails cleanly on both discriminating axes — progression on first-line systemic treatment is required, and ECOG must be 0-1. Sites are in China, which matters only because no geography band was ever elicited from her.

indication: Locally advanced or metastatic osteosarcoma and soft tissue sarcoma
intervention: HS-20093 with anlotinib, epirubicin or adebrelimab
endpoint: Maximum tolerated dose for the combinations
inclusion_match_notes: Worth tracking because one arm does what almost nothing else in the B7-H3 space does — the cohort 1 dose-expansion enrolls patients who have had no prior treatment for advanced disease, and another arm pairs the ADC with an anthracycline. The histology gate is the problem: cohort 1 is soft tissue sarcoma and cohort 2 is osteosarcoma, and chondrosarcoma is named in neither. ECOG 0-1 and a 4-week major-surgery washout apply, and the study had not opened at the time of this screen.

indication: Stage III-IV or recurrent sarcoma with confirmed CAR-T target antigen expression
line: any (at least 2 weeks from last chemotherapy or radiotherapy)
biomarker: surface antigen expression by IHC or flow: GD2, PSMA, HER2, CD276 (B7-H3) or other
design: Open-label phase 1/2, multiple CAR-T products plus low-dose chemotherapy and maintenance vaccine
intervention: Sarcoma-specific CAR-T cells including anti-CD276 (B7-H3), with low-dose chemotherapy and irradiated tumour-cell vaccine
intervention_dosing: 1x10^6 to 1x10^7 CAR-T cells/kg IV single infusion; vaccine 1-5x10^6 irradiated cells SC
inclusion_match_notes: An antigen-gated rather than histology-gated platform: entry turns on IHC or flow confirmation that the tumour expresses one of the listed CAR targets, CD276 among them, and B7-H3 positivity is near-universal in dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma. Two features make it unusually permissive for this patient — Karnofsky 50% or better rather than ECOG 0-1, and no requirement for prior systemic therapy. Set against that: 20 patients, one Chinese site, safety as the primary endpoint, an exclusion for rapidly progressing disease, and lymphodepletion fitness that an unmeasured performance status cannot be assumed to clear.

indication: Advanced solid tumours including sarcoma
biomarker: none required; archival or fresh tissue mandatory
design: First-in-human phase 1/1b dose escalation and cohort expansion
inclusion_match_notes: Sarcoma sits in the enumerated tumour list for this B7-H3 ADC, so the antigen rationale carries over from the dedifferentiated component. The registered criteria say only "adequate performance and laboratory parameters" without a numeric ECOG threshold, which is unusual and means the fitness bar has to be asked of the site rather than read off the record. Tissue is mandatory and major surgery within 4 weeks is exclusionary, both of which interact with a pending stabilisation procedure that could supply the largest specimen available.

indication: Advanced solid tumours
line: 2L+ (progressed on or intolerant to available standard therapy)
design: Phase 1 monotherapy and combination dose escalation and expansion (EMBOLD)
intervention: Risvutatug rezetecan (GSK5764227), B7-H3-directed antibody-drug conjugate, alone or with platinum or checkpoint blockade
inclusion_match_notes: The Western development arm of the same B7-H3 ADC that Hansoh is running as HS-20093, opened as a broad solid-tumour phase 1 with no histology carve-out, which is why it appears here despite no sarcoma-specific cohort. Entry requires progression on or intolerance to all available standard therapy and ECOG 0-1, so it sits well behind first-line chemotherapy for her. Carried mainly so the board sees the B7-H3 pipeline is not a single-sponsor bet.

indication: Advanced clear cell sarcoma, HLA-A*02:01 positive
intervention_dosing: IV weekly with intra-patient dose escalation
sponsor: Sarcoma Alliance for Research through Collaboration (SARC)
inclusion_match_notes: Kept as the reference point for the HLA-restricted platform, which is the axis her untested class I genotype gates: eligibility turns on HLA-A*02:01 and the ECOG bar is 2 or better, the most permissive fitness criterion in this whole screen. The histology is the wall — clear cell sarcoma only, and gp100 is a melanocytic antigen with no expected expression in a cartilage tumour. Her HLA typing is worth drawing regardless, because it is what determines whether any peptide-HLA-directed agent, this one or a future MAGE-A4, NY-ESO-1 or PRAME product, is even discussable.

indication: Advanced soft tissue sarcoma, NY-ESO-1 positive
biomarker: NY-ESO-1 expression; HLA-A*02:01 restriction implicit in the TCR construct
endpoint: Adverse events and serious adverse events
inclusion_match_notes: Allows ECOG 0-2, which almost no cell-therapy protocol does, and gates on antigen expression rather than a named histology — but the enrolling condition is soft tissue sarcoma and a pelvic chondrosarcoma is a bone primary. Both of the tests this would need, HLA class I genotyping and NY-ESO-1 expression on the dedifferentiated component, are still unordered, so the row is unassessable rather than negative. Lymphodepletion fitness is a second bar that an unmeasured performance status cannot be assumed to clear.

indication: Unresectable or R2-resected radioresistant tumours, including chondrosarcoma WHO grade >=2 outside the skull base
design: Transnational randomised trial of carbon-ion therapy versus conventional radiotherapy including protons (ETOILE)
inclusion_match_notes: Chondrosarcoma of WHO grade 2 or above outside the skull base is written into the eligible list, the ECOG bar is 2 or better, and unresectable disease is the point of the trial — so on histology, site and fitness this fits her better than anything else screened. Metastatic disease is an explicit exclusion, and so is disease not a candidate for a curative approach, which is what removes her. The finding to carry is that the radioresistance argument for particle therapy in this disease is being tested in a randomised setting, and that her metastases, not her pelvis, are what disqualify her from it.

indication: Newly diagnosed pelvic sarcoma involving bone, chondrosarcoma named
design: Prospective comparative-effectiveness trial of carbon-ion therapy, surgery and proton therapy
intervention: Carbon-ion radiotherapy, proton therapy or surgery
endpoint: Change in functional outcome; proportion with local recurrence
inclusion_match_notes: Newly diagnosed pelvic chondrosarcoma, ECOG 2 or better, function and local control as the endpoints — the protocol is built around precisely the acetabular problem she has, and it is the one row where her treatment-naive status is an inclusion rather than an obstacle. Distant metastases are an explicit exclusion, so the dispersed lung nodules close it. Its value to the board is the three-way framing of the acetabular decision, surgery against protons against carbon ions, which still has to be made for her outside a protocol.

indication: Pelvic chondrosarcoma
design: Retrospective comparative study of surgery versus carbon-ion radiotherapy
endpoint: Overall survival, local recurrence and Musculoskeletal Tumor Society functional score
effect_size: 5-year OS 72%; local recurrence 32%; mean MSTS score 59%
p_value: 0.347 for OS between modalities; 0.03 favouring CIRT on function
quality: retrospective, small, ROBINS-I serious risk of selection bias
sponsor: Osaka University / National Institute of Radiological Sciences
inclusion_match_notes: Directly on the anatomical question: pelvic chondrosarcoma treated with carbon ions or surgery, with no survival difference between them and better musculoskeletal function after carbon-ion therapy. The cohort was non-metastatic and treated with curative intent, so the survival figures do not transfer to her; what transfers is the local-control and function comparison for a periacetabular lesion, which is the live decision alongside systemic therapy. Small, retrospective, and subject to selection bias in who was offered which modality.

indication: Advanced solid tumours, lymphoma or myeloma with an actionable genomic alteration
line: 2L+ (no longer benefiting from, or no available, standard treatment)
biomarker: genomic alteration matched to a marketed targeted agent, from any CLIA panel
intervention: Marketed targeted agents assigned by genomic match
endpoint: Objective response or stable disease at 16 weeks
inclusion_match_notes: ECOG 0-2 is the criterion that matters here — one of only a handful of open protocols in this screen whose fitness bar an assumed-2 patient clears as written. Everything else waits on the panel: entry requires an actionable alteration matched to a marketed agent, and no comprehensive profiling has been done. The line criterion is soft rather than numeric, phrased as no longer benefiting from or having no available standard treatment, which for a chemo-responsive dedifferentiated tumour realistically places it after first-line anthracycline.

indication: Advanced bone and soft tissue sarcoma with CDK-pathway alteration; dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma named
line: 2L+ for dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma (at least one prior anthracycline required)
biomarker: CCND1/2/3, CDK4 or CDK6 amplification or gain, or CDKN2A/B loss; Rb-positive by central IHC
inclusion_match_notes: Dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma is named in the eligible histologies by itself, and CDKN2A/B loss — one of the recurrent alterations in this subtype and already on the pending panel — is a qualifying biomarker, so this is the clearest post-first-line landing spot found in the screen. Three gates stand between her and it: at least one prior anthracycline for the dedifferentiated group, which first-line treatment would satisfy; central Rb IHC and a documented CDK-pathway alteration, neither ordered; and ECOG 0 or 1, which is stricter than most and is the axis to measure. A 14-day post-surgical window plus no significant wound-healing problems is more forgiving than the usual 4 weeks if stabilisation goes ahead.
